comparator.route: International Communication & Business and Creative Industries & Audiences focus areas with minor
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official 2026-2027 ESHCC Teaching and Examination Regulations and the current official programme pages. The pathway contains 60 EC of mandatory first-year courses; 60 EC of later mandatory theory, methods, practice, internship and thesis work; 20 EC across two focus areas; a 5-EC focus-area research workshop; 20 EC of open electives; and a 15-EC minor. Appendix 8 lists 20 EC of focus areas and 35 EC of electives for the 2026-2027 minor route but itemises only 175 EC despite stating a 180-EC grand total. The current official programme page separately retains a research workshop in year 2. The 5-EC restricted-choice research-workshop component is therefore preserved to reconcile the current official structure and stated total without inventing a workshop title. The generic target does not choose among four focus areas. The first two listed focus areas and the minor route are selected by official order before and independently of UCR course selection. Open electives and the minor remain generic rather than being filled with invented subjects.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest programme, this route removes AI ethics, data science, modern sociology, business and AI, marketing, media archaeology, creative communication, literature-film study and leadership communication. It adds law and justice, comparative politics, international and constitutional law, modern and imperial history, peace and conflict, climate communication and political psychology of extremism. Fifteen courses are shared and nine differ. The organising choice shifts from broad communication-and-media study to the institutions, histories, conflicts and public spheres through which international and political communication operates.

alternatives.concept: A digital media and organisations route combining media history, platforms, entertainment and representation with AI and data, audience and market research, marketing, organisational communication, leadership, entrepreneurship and responsible digital transformation.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest programme, this route removes international relations, EU politics, persuasive communication and style analysis. It adds business foundations, digital strategy, market research and organisational psychology. Twenty courses are shared and four differ, meeting the 30-EC floor exactly. Those changes are not threshold substitutions: they implement the evidenced shift from a broad communication-and-society programme to the organisational production, transformation, marketing and empirical study of digital media and audiences. Only eleven courses are shared with the global-political route.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic IBCoM bachelor. The current regulations provide no basis for treating one of the four focus areas as the defining route. The first two listed focus areas are selected as the neutral official-order tie-break, and the minor route is selected because it is listed before exchange. These choices were made before UCR course selection.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Communication, media and sociology foundations begin in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected marketing course, and introductory media and social theory precede advanced work in persuasive communication, race and media, social theory, documentary, platform media and film-text relations. Later semesters integrate organisations, audiences, public institutions and international relations. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed earlier.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme integrates communication and media theory, media industries, technologies, cultural sociology, rhetoric, mixed methods, digital data, ethics, audiences and public life. Two further generator-backed directions remain coherent and feasible. International and political communication reorganises the field around comparative politics, international relations, law, history, conflict and public debate. Digital media, audiences and organisations reorganises it around platforms, AI, entertainment, consumer engagement, organisational communication, strategy and market research. The closest and political routes share 15 courses; the closest and digital-organisational routes share 20; and the latter two share 11. Every pair clears the 4-course floor, and each difference follows from a distinct evidenced organising logic. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce media as a field of study and examine representation, production, audiences and social influence; UCR includes film more prominently.
Both use social-science theory to analyse culture, social change and power; UCR concentrates on sociological modernity and colonial critique.
Both examine how media are produced and received; UCR approaches these questions through documentary form, institutions, ethics and audiences.
Both analyse communication and institutions as forces shaping collective life; UCR does so through advanced social theory and civil-society research.
Both compare institutional systems across countries; the comparator specialises in media systems, while UCR provides broader comparative-political analysis.
Both study communication technologies historically and critically, including how technical infrastructures shape social practice.
Both examine rapidly changing platforms and digital media; UCR focuses on television, streaming, TikTok and audience change.
Both examine communication across cultural difference and identity; UCR focuses specifically on race, representation and power in media.
Film & Text directly supports the selected creative-industries and audiences focus through narrative, adaptation and cultural representation.
Both examine communication inside organisations and with stakeholders; UCR gives added attention to leadership practice.
Both develop strategic audience analysis and communication planning; UCR centres ethical persuasion and campaign design.
Both develop professional orientation, reflection, communication and portfolio-related skills; UCR embeds these in broader personal and academic development.
Both examine and produce communicative content; UCR uses experimental, sonic, poetic and performative forms rather than only digital marketing and storytelling.
Both address professional ethical responsibility in contemporary communication; UCR specialises in AI, bias, transparency and human consequences.
Marketing & Consumer Engagement directly addresses audience strategy, branding and responsible organisational communication within the selected business focus.
Market Research is an applied research course on audiences and markets, providing a direct counterpart to a focus-area communication research workshop.
Both examine international structures, power and cross-border meaning-making; UCR approaches them through international-relations theory rather than a dedicated communication course.
Both develop quantitative research design, operationalisation and statistical analysis; UCR includes surveys and experiments across business and social questions.
Both teach qualitative research design, data collection, interpretation and reflexive evaluation.
Both develop practical analysis and presentation of quantitative data; UCR emphasises data cleaning and visualisation rather than an SPSS statistics sequence.

The comparator has a dedicated introduction to the full social-science research process. UCR distributes those foundations across Research Methods & Statistics and Qualitative Research Methodology, each already aligned to a more specific later methods component.
The comparator requires a dedicated cross-national communication research workshop. UCR includes comparative content but no scheduled course that independently reproduces this specific workshop.
The comparator requires a 15-EC individual empirical bachelor thesis. No scheduled UCR course is asserted as an equivalent independent thesis.
The comparator requires a 12-EC communication-and-media internship. None of the scheduled UCR courses is a workplace placement.
The comparator preserves 20 EC of open electives. UCR choice is distributed across the complete liberal-arts programme rather than represented by one scheduled course.
The comparator includes a 15-EC approved minor. UCR breadth is distributed across the complete programme rather than contained in a separate minor component.

notes.text: IBCoM provides a continuous specialist sequence in communication and media theory, comparative media systems, quantitative and qualitative communication research, focus-area study, professional workshops, a compulsory internship and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. UCR can build strong pathways across media, rhetoric, sociology, politics, organisations, data and digital change, but it does not reproduce that full disciplinary sequence or mandatory professional placement.
